decision: Finish native integration and packaging with opt-in scoring
why: Human quality evidence is absent; engineering can still be completed without changing the default learner

decision: Use a reusable Rust library loaded from bundled app resources
why: One objective serves Tauri and evaluation; avoids subprocess lifecycle and system-library discovery while leaving default learner available

decision: Use Claude-designed opt-in control with explicit errors
why: Native scoring can be verified before the human quality gate without silent fallback or automatic apply after engine switches

decision: Real native desktop workflow passes 27 assertions
why: Verified actual webview IPC, apply, human decisions, undo, reload and cross-shoot learning without backend stubs

decision: Sign the native dylib before Tauri copies it into signed macOS releases
why: Resource copying alone does not add the library to Tauri signing paths; hardened runtime requires matching signature

decision: Local macOS application bundle loads its copied XGBoost library
why: Checked the library at the actual app resource path and validated keeper ordering and bundled license

decision: Record synthetic latency and native process memory without an adoption verdict
why: Host is busy and no human dataset exists; report raw repeated observations with explicit scope limits
